title: Improve Windows compatibility and connection reliability
body:
## Windows Compatibility and Connection Reliability Improvements

This PR addresses cross-platform compatibility issues and implements robust connection management features:

### Key Features

**Auto-Discovery and Connection Management:**
- Added host and port auto-discovery system
- browser tools server tries port 3025 by default, with fallback to other ports
- Implemented smart server scanning to find running servers across multiple host/port combinations
- Added server identity verification to prevent connecting to incorrect web servers
- Enhanced WebSocket reconnection logic after abnormal closures (excludes codes 1000, 1001, 1005)
- Implemented heartbeat mechanism (30s ping interval) to keep connections alive
- Added intentional closure tracking to prevent unnecessary reconnection attempts

**User Interface Improvements:**
- Added connection status indicators to show when connected/disconnected
- Added server information display (version, host, port)
- Added manual connection configuration options for custom hosts/ports
- Implemented auto-reconnect on page refresh
- Added auto-discover server button for easier setup
- Added connection testing functionality

**Cross-Platform Path Handling:**
- Added comprehensive path conversion for Windows/Linux/macOS compatibility
- Fixed screenshot path handling for Windows systems
- Added WSL path detection and conversion

**Code Improvements:**
- Improved cleanup on DevTools window closed
- Enhanced error handling throughout the codebase
- Reduced console noise from heartbeat messages
- Proper cleanup of timers/intervals to prevent memory leaks

### Testing

Tested on:
- Windows 10/11
- macOS
- Various network configurations

This PR addresses user feedback about Windows compatibility issues and connection problems reported in earlier releases.

title: Chrome Extension fails to establish WebSocket connection with Node server
body:
## Environment
- OS: macOS (darwin 22.6.0)
- Chrome Extension Version: 1.0.0
- MCP Server Version: 1.0.11
- Node Server Status: Running (confirmed via ps aux)

## Issue Description
The Chrome extension fails to establish a WebSocket connection with the Node server, resulting in "fetch failed" responses for all MCP tool calls.

## Observed Behavior
1. MCP server logs show successful processing of requests
2. All tool calls (getConsoleLogs, takeScreenshot, etc.) return "fetch failed"
3. No WebSocket connections or errors visible in Chrome DevTools Network tab
4. Extension shows "Can't Read or Change Site's Data" in popup menu
5. Node server processes are running correctly:
   ```
   PID 31500: node /Users/my.name/.npm/_npx/7c39ed364bc7f6f8/node_modules/.bin/browser-tools-mcp
   PID 31485: npm exec @agentdeskai/browser-tools-mcp@1.0.11
   PID 31484: npx @agentdeskai/browser-tools-mcp@1.0.11
   ```

## Configuration
1. Extension has all required permissions:
   - Access to all sites
   - JavaScript allowed
   - Background sync enabled
   - Camera and Window management explicitly allowed
2. Extension is properly installed and enabled
3. Node server is running and accessible

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install and configure browser-tools-mcp
2. Run the Node server via npx
3. Install Chrome extension
4. Attempt to use any MCP tool (e.g., takeScreenshot, getConsoleLogs)
5. Observe "fetch failed" response despite server logs showing successful processing

## Expected Behavior
- WebSocket connection should establish between Chrome extension and Node server
- MCP tools should return actual data from the browser

## Additional Notes
- No errors appear in Chrome DevTools console
- Extension permissions and configuration appear correct
- Node server logs indicate it's receiving requests successfully
- The disconnect appears to be in the communication between the Chrome extension and Node server
